Return the original label Entailment (supported), Contradiction (opposed), or NotMentioned (not settled by the document); do not substitute external law for contractual text. Decide the relation relative to the exact original hypothesis, including its negation, not whether the contract contains a prohibition. The same 17 hypotheses are checked on every document. All original text is present, with zero-based original span markers <SPAN i>...</SPAN i>. For supported/opposed hypotheses cite all original evidence span indices for that decision, including independently operative redundant support and necessary governing language. For NotMentioned return an empty evidence list. Treat conditions and exceptions within scope, and distinguish limited permission from universal permission. Give a short public reason (at most 15 words per hypothesis). Do not execute further tools, invent citations or rewrite span indices. Return exactly the supplied JSON schema with all 17 original hypothesis keys. For each emit choice, spans, reason in that order. The common schema describes permitted values, not answers about this contract. Evidence candidates are fallible, not mandatory citations; make every final label and evidence decision yourself from the complete original contract. The complete original NDA remains present and unchanged. Each hypothesis has fallible_evidence_candidates from a fixed ordinary retriever, plus additional_source_read_indices obtained by literal source access. Both resolve to exact original text in candidate_original_text. Additional indices omit duplicate ordinary candidates, not low-scoring facts. These are reading aids, never a verdict or mandatory evidence. Scores describe fallible evidence membership, not legal confidence. No skill identities, query counts or scope-control map are supplied. Optional evidence_selection_criteria are fallible learned inspection procedures for that hypothesis, never contract facts, label verdicts or mandatory citations. Literal access roles describe how a location was reached, not whether it is evidence. Empty leads never mean NotMentioned. Read the full source, reject irrelevant material and cite ANY original index as needed, including outside every lead. Decide the exact original hypothesis yourself; do not substitute another hypothesis. Return choice, spans and reason only.

{"full_contract_with_original_span_markers":"<SPAN 0>WECC </SPAN 0><SPAN 1>Confidentiality Agreement</SPAN 1>
<SPAN 2>This WECC Confidentiality Agreement (“Agreement”) is entered into by </SPAN 2><SPAN 3>__________________________ </SPAN 3><SPAN 4>(“Data Recipient”) and is effective as of the date agreed to by Data Recipient. </SPAN 4><SPAN 5>Data Recipient agrees to the following terms and conditions pertaining to Non-Public Information.</SPAN 5>
<SPAN 6>1. Non-Public Information</SPAN 6>
<SPAN 7>a. Non-Public Information shall include any and all information Data Recipient receives from WECC, including, but not limited to, information received through a login to the WECC website, which:</SPAN 7>
<SPAN 8>i. Is designated as “Confidential Information” or “Market Sensitive Information” or is otherwise considered non-public under the WECC Information Sharing Policy;</SPAN 8>
<SPAN 9>ii. Meets the definition of Confidential Information as set forth in Section 1500 of the North American Electric Reliability Corporation Rules of Procedure; or</SPAN 9>
<SPAN 10>iii. Is identified by WECC as non-public or confidential at the time of disclosure.</SPAN 10>
<SPAN 11>b. For the purposes of this Agreement, Non-Public Information shall not include:</SPAN 11>
<SPAN 12>i. Information that is or becomes available in the public domain through no fault or action of Data Recipient;</SPAN 12>
<SPAN 13>ii. Information that was or is acquired by Data Recipient from a source other than WECC in a manner which is not otherwise subject to confidentiality restrictions; or</SPAN 13>
<SPAN 14>iii. Information that was or is independently developed by Data Recipient as demonstrated by Data Recipient’s documentation.</SPAN 14>
<SPAN 15>2. Treatment of Non-Public Information</SPAN 15>
<SPAN 16>a. Data Recipient agrees to take all necessary precautions to maintain the confidentiality of the Non-Public Information and to prevent unauthorized access to it.</SPAN 16>
<SPAN 17>b. Data Recipient agrees to not make available, disclose, provide or communicate Non-Public Information to any entity or individual, except:</SPAN 17>
<SPAN 18>i. Employees of Data Recipient who </SPAN 18><SPAN 19>(1) have signed an acknowledgment of this Agreement or a non-disclosure agreement that covers the Non-Public Information and is at least as restrictive as this Agreement, and </SPAN 19><SPAN 20>(2) need the Non-Public Information for performance of a job function subject to the limitation on Market Sensitive Information below;</SPAN 20>
<SPAN 21>ii. Contractors of Data Recipient who </SPAN 21><SPAN 22>(1) have signed a non-disclosure agreement that covers the Non-Public Information and is at least as restrictive as this Agreement, and </SPAN 22><SPAN 23>(2) need the Non-Public Information for the work being performed subject to the limitation on Market Sensitive Information below. </SPAN 23><SPAN 24>In the event Data Recipient shares Non-Public Information with a contractor pursuant to this provision, Data Recipient agrees to be responsible and jointly and severally liable for any breach of confidentiality by that contractor;</SPAN 24>
<SPAN 25>iii. As required by FERC orders, rules or regulations, provided that additional data recipients have signed a non-disclosure agreement that covers the Non-Public Information and is at least as restrictive as this Agreement; or</SPAN 25>
<SPAN 26>iv. As may be otherwise agreed to by WECC in writing.</SPAN 26>
<SPAN 27>3. Market Sensitive Information</SPAN 27>
<SPAN 28>a. Data Recipient agrees not to provide or disclose any Market Sensitive Information as identified in the WECC Information Sharing Policy to any person who is </SPAN 28><SPAN 29>(1) a Market Function Employee as defined by the FERC Standards of Conduct, or </SPAN 29><SPAN 30>(2) actively and personally engaged in day-to-day sales of electric power or other electric power marketing functions.</SPAN 30>
<SPAN 31>4. Compelled Disclosures</SPAN 31>
<SPAN 32>a. Notwithstanding anything to the contrary herein, </SPAN 32><SPAN 33>Data Recipient may disclose Non-Public Information to a governmental authority as required by law, provided that to the extent permitted by law:</SPAN 33>
<SPAN 34>i. Data Recipient notifies WECC as soon as reasonably possible of the required disclosure;</SPAN 34>
<SPAN 35>ii. Data Recipient does not disclose the Non-Public Information until WECC has had a reasonable opportunity to respond to the required disclosure; and</SPAN 35>
<SPAN 36>iii. Data Recipient cooperates with WECC as reasonably requested by WECC to protect WECC’s interests in the Non-Public Information.</SPAN 36>
<SPAN 37>b. If Data Recipient is an entity subject to state or federal freedom of information laws or an employee of such an entity, Data Recipient certifies that the Non-Public Information is eligible for restriction from public disclosure and agrees to:</SPAN 37>
<SPAN 38>i. Restrict the Non-Public Information from public disclosure;</SPAN 38>
<SPAN 39>ii. Notify WECC as soon as reasonably possible of any request for the Non-Public Information; and</SPAN 39>
<SPAN 40>iii. Cooperate with WECC as reasonably requested by WECC to protect WECC’s interests in the Non-Public Information.</SPAN 40>
<SPAN 41>5. Disclaimer and Limitations</SPAN 41>
<SPAN 42>a. Neither WECC nor any owner or submitter of the Non-Public Information makes any representation or warranty as to the completeness, accuracy, relevance, or usability of the Non-Public Information. </SPAN 42><SPAN 43>All Non-Public Information made available to Data Recipient is made available AS IS AND WITHOUT WARRANTY, EXPRESS OR IMPLIED.</SPAN 43>
<SPAN 44>b. There is no obligation on the part of WECC or any owner or submitter of the Non-Public Information to supplement, update, or correct any Non-Public Information, even if the Non-Public Information is supplemented, updated, or corrected for other purposes.</SPAN 44>
<SPAN 45>c. Use of the Non-Public Information is at Data Recipient’s own risk. </SPAN 45><SPAN 46>Neither WECC nor the owner or submitter of the Non-Public Information shall be liable for any damages arising out of the use of the Non-Public Information.</SPAN 46>
<SPAN 47>6. Changes in Employment</SPAN 47>
<SPAN 48>a. If at any time during the term of this Agreement Data Recipient or an employee of Data Recipient ceases to be employed by his or her then current employer, Data Recipient agrees to notify WECC within five (5) business days of the change in employment.</SPAN 48>
<SPAN 49>b. If at any time during the term of this Agreement Data Recipient or an employee of Data Recipient has a change in job responsibilities such that Data Recipient or an employee of Data Recipient becomes a Market Function Employee, Data Recipient agrees to notify WECC within five (5) business days of the change in employment and to ensure that Data Recipient or such an employee of Data Recipient discontinues accessing or using any Market Sensitive Information as identified in the WECC Information Sharing Policy.</SPAN 49>
<SPAN 50>7. Term and Termination</SPAN 50>
<SPAN 51>a. This Agreement shall continue in effect until terminated. </SPAN 51><SPAN 52>This Agreement may be terminated by WECC or Data Recipient at any time at their sole discretion.</SPAN 52>
<SPAN 53>b. Upon any termination of this Agreement, Data Recipient shall return to WECC all Non-Public Information in Data Recipient’s possession or destroy all Non-Public Information in Data Recipient’s possession and certify to WECC in writing that all Non-Public Information has been returned or destroyed, except as may be otherwise required by law in which case the confidentiality obligations of this Agreement shall survive termination.</SPAN 53>
<SPAN 54>8. Miscellaneous </SPAN 54><SPAN 55>Terms</SPAN 55>
<SPAN 56>a. This Agreement does not require WECC to disclose any Non-Public Information. </SPAN 56><SPAN 57>Neither this Agreement nor any disclosure of Non-Public Information grant Data Recipient any intellectual property rights or licenses to such information. </SPAN 57><SPAN 58>Data Recipient agrees to comply with all applicable United States export laws and regulations.</SPAN 58>
<SPAN 59>b. This Agreement represents the entire understanding between WECC and Data Recipient related to the Non-Public Information and supersedes all previous communications between WECC and Data Recipient related to this subject. </SPAN 59><SPAN 60>This Agreement can only be modified by written agreement executed by WECC and Data Recipient. </SPAN 60><SPAN 61>Data </SPAN 61><SPAN 62>Recipient may not delegate its duties or obligations under this Agreement without prior written consent from WECC. </SPAN 62><SPAN 63>Any attempt to do so is void.</SPAN 63>
<SPAN 64>c. This Agreement shall be for the sole benefit of WECC and any owner or submitter of the Non-Public Information. </SPAN 64><SPAN 65>This Agreement shall be fully enforceable by WECC and any entity whose Non-Public Information is not treated in accordance with this Agreement.</SPAN 65>
<SPAN 66>d. If any term or provision of this Agreement is held by a body of competent jurisdiction to be invalid, void, or unenforceable, then </SPAN 66><SPAN 67>(1) the remaining provisions of the Agreement shall continue in full force and effect, and </SPAN 67><SPAN 68>(2) in lieu of each such term or provision there shall be added as part of this Agreement a clause or provision as similar in terms as possible that is legal, valid and enforceable.</SPAN 68>
<SPAN 69>IN WITNESS HEREOF, Data Recipient has read and understands this Agreement and enters into this Agreement voluntarily, wishing to be legally bound.</SPAN 69>
<SPAN 70>Data Recipient</SPAN 70>
